name: ssis-lineage
description: Scan SSIS projects and visualize / trace column-level data lineage inside VS Code.

languageModelTools.name: ssisLineage_search
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search the scanned SSIS project for columns or tables by name (substring match). Returns matching fully-qualified names. Requires a prior scan.

term.description: Substring to search for, e.g. a column or table name.

languageModelTools.name: ssisLineage_trace
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Trace data lineage for a column or table in the scanned SSIS project. direction 'upstream' returns origins/sources, 'downstream' returns impact/targets, 'both' returns the full path. Returns ordered hops (source -> target with operation). Requires a prior scan.

target.description: Column or table to trace, e.g. 'DW.Dim_Customers.Email' or 'DW.Dim_Customers'.

direction.description: upstream = origins, downstream = impact, both = full path (default).

languageModelTools.name: ssisLineage_status
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Report whether an SSIS project has been scanned and loaded in this session, with counts (packages, tasks, components, column mappings).

ssisLineage.cliPath.markdownDescription: Path to the SSIS Lineage CLI — either a self-contained executable, or a `SsisLineage.Cli.dll` (run via `dotnet`). Leave empty to use a binary bundled with the extension. For development, point this at the built CLI, e.g. `…/src/SsisLineage.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/SsisLineage.Cli.dll`.

ssisLineage.startPackage.description: Entry/master package to scan from (e.g. Master.dtsx). When empty, you are prompted to pick one from the project.

ssisLineage.includeSqlProcedures.description: Connect to SQL Server and resolve stored-procedure lineage for data-flow components. On by default so procedure-backed sources trace through to their source tables; turn off for a faster package/XML-only scan with no database connection.

ssisLineage.sqlConnectionString.markdownDescription: SQL Server connection string used only when 'Include SQL Procedures' is enabled. Prefer the **SSIS Lineage: Set SQL Connection…** command, which stores the string in VS Code Secret Storage instead of plaintext settings. This setting (if non-empty) takes precedence; otherwise the stored secret is used, then the project's `.conmgr` connection managers.

ssisLineage.connectionManagerOverrides.markdownDescription: Per-connection-manager connection-string overrides, keyed by connection-manager **name or GUID** (e.g. `{ "Staging": "Server=…;Database=Staging;Integrated Security=true", "DW": "Server=…;Database=DW;Integrated Security=true" }`). Redirects specific `.conmgr` connections; the single connection (setting/secret) remains the fallback for any not listed. Note: values are stored in settings — use Integrated Security where possible to avoid plaintext credentials.
